what_it_is.prose: TARA is an indigenous Indian GPS/INS-guided glide bomb designed by the Armament and Research Development Establishment (ARDE) of DRDO in Pune. The weapon is a stand-off precision strike munition that, once released from a fighter aircraft at altitude, glides autonomously to its target using GPS/INS guidance with an optional terminal seeker for enhanced accuracy. With an estimated stand-off range of approximately 100 km, TARA gives Indian fighter aircraft the ability to engage fixed ground targets from outside the range of most short- and medium-range air defence systems. The glide bomb carries a high-explosive warhead in the 100-200 kg class. TARA has been tested from the Su-30MKI and is planned for integration on the Tejas. The programme is in the tested/procurement phase, with the Indian Air Force evaluating the weapon for operational induction.

faq.question: What is a glide bomb?
faq.answer: A glide bomb is an unpowered, precision-guided munition that, once released from an aircraft at altitude, glides autonomously to its target using GPS/INS and optional terminal guidance. Unlike powered missiles, glide bombs have no engine — they rely on altitude and aerodynamic lift to reach their target, giving them a stand-off range of tens to hundreds of kilometres. They are a cost-effective alternative to powered cruise missiles for strikes against fixed ground targets.

faq.question: How does TARA compare to the Israeli Spice guidance kit?
faq.answer: The Spice guidance kit converts unguided bombs into precision-guided weapons with GPS/INS + electro-optical terminal guidance and ~60-100 km range. TARA is a purpose-built indigenous glide bomb with similar GPS/INS guidance and ~100 km range, but is designed as a complete weapon system rather than a conversion kit. TARA offers an indigenous alternative to imported Spice kits, reducing long-term import dependence.

faq.question: What is the TARA glide weapon?
faq.answer: TARA is India's first indigenous modular glide weapon system, jointly developed by DRDO and the Indian Air Force. It is an attachable wing-and-guidance kit that converts standard bombs into precision-guided glide weapons, so an aircraft can release them from stand-off distances.

faq.question: Has TARA been tested?
faq.answer: DRDO and the IAF conducted the maiden flight trial of the TARA glide weapon in 2026, demonstrating that the attachable kit allows missiles and bombs to fly longer and strike targets with greater accuracy, validating the indigenous design toward induction.
